messages.subject: Beginners question
parts:
I have a data frame "x" like this:

PID Adapt Ecc N1Amp N1IT P1Amp P1IT N2Amp N2IT Timep
1 ak pre 1 1.600 1.58 2.93 3.170 2.28 4.75 -3

and following code:

#-------------
mkplot <- function (xdat, var, xlstr, ylstr, fn)
{
p <- ggplot(xdat) +
geom_line(aes(Timep,var,group=PID)) +
geom_point(aes(Timep,var,colour=PID)) +
scale_x_continuous(name=xlstr) +
scale_y_continuous(name=ylstr) +
facet_grid(. ~ Ecc)
theme_set(theme_bw())
ggsave(file=fn,width=10, height=3)
}

mkplot(x,'N1Amp','x','y','N1Amp.eps')
#---------------

Unfortunately this code does not work due to a problem with "var". So
how do i pass the data frame column name to the function or how do i
refer to it within ggplot?

Thanks
Herbert

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Beginners question
parts:
Hi,

I think you want to use aes_string(). Try this,

d <- data.frame(PID = sample(c("ak", "bk"), 10, repl=T),
Adapt = sample(c("pre", "pre2"), 10, repl=T),
Ecc = rnorm(10),
N1Amp = rnorm(10),
N1IT =rnorm(10),
P1Amp=rnorm(10),
P1IT =rnorm(10),
N2Amp=rnorm(10),
N2IT =rnorm(10),
Timep = seq(1, 10))

str(d) # (btw, can you please provide dummy data next time?)


mkplot <- function (dat=d, y="N1Amp", xlab="x", ylab="y"){
p <-
ggplot(dat) +
geom_line( aes_string(x="Timep", y=y, group="PID"))+
geom_point(aes_string(x="Timep", y=y, colour="PID"))+
scale_x_continuous(name=xlab) +
scale_y_continuous(name=ylab) +
facet_grid(. ~ Ecc) +
theme_bw()
print(p)
}

mkplot()
